### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific policy found. The only journal instructions readable are the 2022 Wayback copy, which predates the publisher policy and contains none; the publisher-wide Taylor & Francis policy applies, and it tells authors to check a journal's own instructions because some journals allow AI only for language improvement |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with a disclosure statement |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Publisher policy: generative AI tools must not be listed as authors. Any use must be acknowledged in the article with the tool name and version, how it was used and why. Permitted uses include idea generation, copyediting, language improvement, translation, literature classification and coding assistance. Generating text or code without rigorous revision, synthetic data replacing missing data without a robust method, and AI creation or manipulation of research outputs are prohibited or high-risk. Editors and reviewers may not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

## Format

> Source for the general rules: the instructions for authors, Wayback copy dated 2022-08-08 (https://web.archive.org/web/20220808212457/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rjec20); the live page returns HTTP 403, so current wording may differ. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The instructions copy lists one type: original articles; manuscripts in English only. The aims text also describes symposia and mini-symposia, and a regular book review section with book review symposia (aims copy dated 2022-06-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20220615120353/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=aimsScope&journalCode=rjec20). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-2026: 142 articles, 33 book reviews, 4 editorials, 1 erratum, 1 letter |
| **Word limit** | A typical paper should be no more than 8000 words (instructions copy); the 2026 special-issue call gives 8,000 words as the maximum (https://groups.google.com/g/esa-announce/c/N5kWn8H_KFo) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions word it as a typical-paper ceiling; no statement on exceptions found |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 150 words; no more than 6 keywords (instructions copy) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found. Whether references count inside 8000 words is not stated. References follow a publisher reference guide that the copy links without naming a style in the text read |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, dataset, files) is published online via Figshare (instructions copy) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figure resolution (1200 dpi line art, 600 dpi grayscale, 300 dpi colour), editable tables and editable equations are required (instructions copy) |
| **Style / submission format** | Any spelling style if consistent; single quotation marks; Word or LaTeX (LaTeX also as PDF plus source files); ScholarOne submission; Crossref similarity screening of all submissions; unstructured generic structure (title page, abstract, keywords, main text, acknowledgments, declaration of interest, references) (instructions copy) |

### Orientation

> Counts in this section come from 181 OpenAlex records of 2021-2026, of which 149 carry an abstract (82.3%: article 136 of 142, book review 10 of 33, editorial 2 of 4, erratum 1 of 1; by year 2021: 42 of 47, 2022: 20 of 26, 2023: 20 of 25, 2024: 15 of 21, 2025: 29 of 34, 2026: 23 of 28). Abstracts were rebuilt from OpenAlex's inverted index, and each regex was tested on title plus abstract of those 149 records (patterns in the regex register in AI-Research Notes; names in code font below). Crossref holds no abstracts for this journal (0 of 185 records), so it was used only for the earliest-record date and the record count. Retrieved 2026-11-23. Important caveat: in a journal about the methodology of economics, a keyword such as "econometric" or "experiment" often marks what an article is about, not the method it uses, so the counts describe subject matter as much as method.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Conceptual and normative argument predominates by count: `methodology` terms 70 of 149 (47.0%), `normative_conceptual` 49 (32.9%), `model` 59 (39.6%); `empirical` 24 (16.1%), `causal` 18 (12.1%), `econometric` 12 (8.1%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | `experiment` 10 of 149 (6.7%), `survey` 2 (1.3%), against `qualitative` 3 (2.0%), `case_study` 4 (2.7%) and `mixed_methods` 3 (2.0%); `historical` 16 (10.7%) and `sociological_rhetoric` 9 (6.0%) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | By the journal's own aims it covers philosophy of natural and social science and ethics "as long as they have a direct bearing" on its two fields (aims copy dated 2022-06-15). Primary topics above include philosophy of biology and scientific explanation (14), causal inference techniques (7), scientometrics (5) and feminist epistemology (5) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, one scope condition stated by the journal: it covers economic methodology and philosophy of economics, and it publishes work from any area of economic inquiry only if it contains a significant epistemological or methodological component (home copy dated 2025-11-23, https://web.archive.org/web/20251123103128/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rjec20; same text in the aims copy dated 2022-06-15). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** The aims distinguish methodology (how economics relates to broad questions about scientific knowledge) from methods (techniques particular to a specific field of economics) and reserve the journal's pages for authors and readers with broader epistemic interests (same pages). Topics named include methodological analysis of contemporary economics, philosophical foundations, early economists' methodological writings, causality, explanation and testing, science studies, and the tools and technologies of research in economics.
- **Philosophy of science and ethics** are included only where they have a direct bearing on debates within the two primary fields (same pages).
- **Article types**: original articles in the instructions copy; the aims also mention symposia and book reviews (https://web.archive.org/web/20220808212457/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rjec20). A 2026 special-issue call names topics from replication and experimental methods to behavioural public policy (https://groups.google.com/g/esa-announce/c/N5kWn8H_KFo).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and the only SciRev entry is a single immediate rejection with no stated reason (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-economic-methodology/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are OpenAlex records of this source dated 2021-2026 whose title or abstract matches the stated regex name (case-insensitive unless the register says case-sensitive; word-boundary anchored; patterns in the register in AI-Research Notes); denominator = the 149 records that carry an abstract. Thresholds are this research pass's own convention, not an external standard: share 0 = score 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; scores of 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a term appears, not how a reviewer would treat it, and in a methodology journal many hits describe the subject studied rather than the method used. ### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |

| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. The instructions copy (2022-08-08) points to the publisher's general publishing-ethics guidance and has no journal-specific ethics-approval rule; its data-sharing policy mentions protection of human subjects only as a limit on sharing (https://web.archive.org/web/20220808212457/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rjec20) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author work is the norm: 127 of 181 OpenAlex records have one author (70.2%) (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:1350-178X,publication_year:2021-2026), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The instructions copy asks for full name and affiliation on the cover page, defined as where the research was conducted; no independent-scholar rule is stated (same instructions copy). Review is double-blind (Peer Review) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Encouraged, not required: the journal applies the publisher's Basic Data Sharing Policy; authors are encouraged to share data and cite data sets, and submitters are asked whether a data set exists (instructions copy dated 2022-08-08) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind review, with names and affiliations on the cover page; a manuscript already on a preprint server loses any anonymity guarantee (instructions copy). Pre-submission preprints are allowed by the publisher (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/), retrieved 2026-11-23 |

| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no submission fees, publication fees or page charges, and print colour figures are charged (GBP 300 per figure at the date of the 2022 instructions copy); the APC for open access was not read (instructions copy) |
| **Originality screening** | All submissions are screened for unoriginal material with Crossref similarity checking (instructions copy) |

The method-row scores use the pass's own thresholds stated under Methodological Preferences.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal covers economic methodology and philosophy of economics, and publishes work from other areas of economic inquiry only with a significant epistemological or methodological component (Framing Requirements; archived home and aims text). The aims distinguish "methods" (techniques particular to one field of economics) from methodology and say the pages are reserved for authors and readers with broader epistemic interests, so a paper that only applies a technique within one field, without that component, is outside the stated scope.
- **Article type**: the instructions copy lists original articles as the type accepted (Format; 2022-08-08 copy). Book reviews and symposia appear in the aims text, but how to propose them is not stated in any copy read.
- **Length**: a typical paper should not exceed 8000 words; the 2026 call sets 8,000 as the maximum (Format; Special issues). Whether references count is not stated.
- **Language and anonymity**: English only, and review is double-blind; a manuscript already on a preprint server loses any anonymity guarantee (Format, Peer Review, Preprint Policy).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use breaches the publisher's disclosure rule (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; the instructions are a 2022 copy and ethics-approval rules are unknown (Practical Concerns blank).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no verified turnaround figure exists. A search summary of the unreadable live page gave about 102 days to first decision, which stays unverified; SciRev's single entry is a 72-day immediate rejection (Review Cycle Time).
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript for a non-open-access article is subject to a typical 18-month embargo at the publisher level (Preprint Policy; not confirmed for this journal); gold open access via Open Select carries an APC whose amount was not found (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation**: double-blind review, with a preprint removing any anonymity guarantee (Peer Review, Practical Concerns).
- **Print colour**: colour figures in print are charged (Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual and methodological analysis of economics: `methodology` terms in 70 of 149 abstract-bearing records and `normative_conceptual` in 49 (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Historical, sociological or rhetorical studies of economics, which the aims name explicitly: `historical` 16 and `sociological_rhetoric` 9 of 149 (Methodological Preferences).
- Modelling, rationality and behavioural economics approached from a methodological angle: `model` 59, `rationality` 34 of 149 (Orientation, Sensitive Topics).
- Single-authored work: 127 of 181 records have one author (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Applied empirical or econometric studies with no epistemological or methodological component: the aims separate "methods" from "methodology" and reserve the pages for the latter (Framing Requirements). Hits for `econometric`, `causal` and `empirical` in the counts (8.1%, 12.1% and 16.1%) are best read as papers about those practices, not papers that apply them.
- Authors who need a verified turnaround or acceptance figure before submitting: none is published on any page read (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
- Topics with no appearances in the 149 abstracts: race, colonialism and indigenous topics 0, religion 0 (Sensitive Topics); this shows absence from the sample, not editorial refusal.

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share subject area (philosophy and methodology of economics and social science); they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Economics and Philosophy](economics-and-philosophy.md) | Same two-discipline subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. Its aims text excludes historical or text-interpretive work unless it bears on current debates, so fit for historical papers is weaker (that entry, Framing Requirements) |
| 2 | [Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics](../philosophy/erasmus-journal-for-philosophy-and-economics-ejpe.md) | Same subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Philosophy of the Social Sciences](../philosophy/philosophy-of-the-social-sciences.md) | Philosophy of social science neighbour; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
